dek.text: Texas created a required authorization for commercial driverless vehicles after autonomous freight was already operating. A Senate hearing asks what deployment has meant for safety.

introduction.text: Texas senators are preparing to examine driverless vehicles that are already on the road. The [Transportation Committee's charge](c3) asks how deployment has proceeded under the state's authorization law and what it has meant for traffic collisions.

The Department of Motor Vehicles says the law created a required authorization for commercial driverless operation. That requirement took effect after Aurora announced regular driverless freight deliveries between Dallas and Houston.

paragraphs.text: [Waymo announced](c11) that its Houston robotaxi service had opened to the general public. Kodiak described driverless hauling for Atlas Energy Solutions in Permian Basin oil fields. Aurora described a network of driverless freight routes.

These are company accounts of distinct services. A passenger trip, an oil-field load and a highway freight delivery are not interchangeable measures of deployment. The companies' mileage and load figures don't establish comparative safety by themselves.

sections.heading: The safety question needs a denominator

paragraphs.text: The federal automated-driving incident dataset identifies reporting entities and report types. Texas DPS publishes first-responder interaction information without an incident count on that page. The state's crash-data page does not name a separate automated-driving category.

Those records do not, on their own, answer the committee's request to quantify collision effects. Counting deployments and counting incident reports are different tasks. A safety comparison needs evidence that links the relevant operations to the outcomes being measured.

The Legislature lists a public hearing and asks for recommendations on continued deployment and public safety. The charge is a request for findings. It is not itself a finding that the existing authorization system has made travel safer.
